newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa, United in cargo deal.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa, United in cargo deal.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it has launched a global cargo partnership with United Airlines including joint rates and common sales and marketing.
The deal aims to give the two airlines a stronger leadership position in the air cargo industry, the wholly owned Lufthansa subsiary said.
The two airlines will offer a joint cargo services network on existing services between Europe and North America from November and gradually extend it worldwide.

In an initial test phase, Lufthansa Cargo and United sales staff in Paris and San Francisco are jointly selling space between the two destinations at an agreed rate on Lufthansa and United aircraft, Lufthansa Cargo spokesman Dietrich Seidl said.
Ex-Paris cargo can be carried on the daily United direct San Francisco passenger flight using a Boeing 767 aircraft or trucked to Frankfurt for transport on the daily Lufthansa freighter service.
Cargo out of San Francisco can similarly be sold on the United passenger flight or on the Lufthansa freighter via Frankfurt.

In a joint letter to staff, Lufthansa Cargo Chairman Wilhelm Althen and United Worldwide Cargo Vice President Jim Hartigan said the companies had been discussing a partnership since the granting of U.S. anti-trust immunity on May 22.
Referring to the Paris and San Francisco test, they said, "This is just a starting point, allowing us to offer our customers joint networks between the U.S. and Europe.

"Our partnership, which entails the joint marketing, pricing and selling of our products, will be expanded to the rest of North America and Europe in November, with further global expansion to follow."
The cargo alliance would ensure the future profitability of both companies and provide a unique combination of cargo and passenger products and services, they added.
Lufthansa and United are also investigating joint cargo handling at different stations.
Seidl said, "We did not want to start with Frankfurt or Chicago because of the large volumes. We selected these markets to see how it works in practice."
The two airlines were currently linking computer reservations systems to allow mutual bookings, he added.
There was no change to the cargo capacity offered by the two airlines between Paris and San Francisco, Seidl noted.
No dates have yet been set for the expansion of joint sales and marketing outside Europe and North America.
